title: The daemon serves the preview receipt and its captured screenshot bytes over authenticated read routes
description:
LEAF ROW filed by architect-b63fabf3 on 2026-09-06 at governor-afbde490's 14:44Z direction (option (b) of the waiver). Consumer is task-33ceae56edc348e9864bc592430fa1d0, which declares dependsOn against this row. The leaf was asked for at 13:42Z and 13:55Z and never filed - that delay is the architect team's, mine included: I noted the gap in a 14:33Z census and did not file it.

THE GAP, measured at HEAD by worker-1d53e70c and re-verified by me:
- `grep -c "preview" apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-read-dispatch.ts` returns **ZERO**. There are ~25 read routes and not one serves a preview.
- The `preview.decide` offer is a bare envelope (affordance-planning-offers.ts:143-160: commandEnvelopeVersion, commandId, commandKind, expectedVersion, inputSchemaVersion, targetAggregateId). No url, no screenshots.
- `/activity/read` is an exact 7-key shape carrying VERDICTS only - enough for the consumer's DoD 2, nothing for the receipt.
- The runs read carries no preview member.
So the consumer's DoD 1 (render the loopback URL as a link and the captured screenshots inline) is unreachable from the browser today.

THE FACTS EXIST DURABLY AND MUST BE READ, NOT RE-DERIVED. `PreviewReceiptV1` (preview-receipt-contracts.ts:57-68) already carries exactly what the card needs: `url` (string|null), `screenshots` (readonly PreviewScreenshot[]), `outcome` ("REFUSED"|"STARTED"), `code` (PreviewCode|null), plus goalId, sha, pid, receiptId, decidedAt, projectId, version. `readPreviewReceipt` is the production read surface. This row projects and serves; it computes no new authority.

TWO ROUTES, TWO DIFFERENT SHAPES - and the second is why this is a leaf rather than two steps on the consumer:
1. A JSON read serving the receipt for a goalId, exact-key, alongside the other `/*/read` routes.
2. A READ-ONLY CAPTURE ROUTE serving the screenshot BYTES, confined to `.moe-next/previews/<goalId>/<sha>/` (preview-capture.ts:16 documents that layout, and the receipt decoder already validates paths against it).

**ROUTE 2 IS SECURITY-BOUNDARY WORK.** Serving files from disk to a browser needs path-traversal refusal, root confinement, type and size limits. The listener already has that vocabulary - `LISTENER_ASSET_PATH_TRAVERSAL`, `LISTENER_ASSET_OUTSIDE_ROOT`, `LISTENER_ASSET_ROOT_LEAKS_SECRET`, `LISTENER_ASSET_SEGMENT_INVALID`, `LISTENER_ASSET_TOO_LARGE`, `LISTENER_ASSET_TYPE_UNKNOWN` and five more at http-listener-guards.ts:31-41. REUSE that machinery; do not write a second file server. The consumer row could NOT host this: its inherited rail 4 is "FEATURES ONLY: no security-boundary or policy work", and the governor's waiver covered its rail 1 only.

NOT IN SCOPE: the Needs-you card, the approve/reject controls, the status strip, the refusal words, the Playwright journey, the live drive and the docs - all task-33ceae56's.

VERIFICATION COMMAND for moe.complete_task: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`. Also `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` (the proxy roster arm lives there) and `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file.
definitionOfDone: An authenticated JSON read serves the preview receipt for a goalId: `url`, `screenshots[]`, `outcome` and `code` at minimum, projected from `PreviewReceiptV1` through the production read surface (`readPreviewReceipt`), never re-derived. The response is an EXACT-key shape and a goal with no receipt reads as absent rather than refusing. Assert the served values against a receipt written by the real preview path, not a hand-built one.

A READ-ONLY capture route serves the screenshot bytes and is CONFINED to `.moe-next/previews/<goalId>/<sha>/`. REUSE the listener's existing asset guards (http-listener-guards.ts:31-41) rather than writing a second file server: assert traversal (`..`, absolute paths, encoded separators, a symlink pointing outside the root) is REFUSED with the specific rostered code, and that a path inside the root is served. One arm per refusal class, each asserting the CODE, never merely that it failed.

THE ROUTE SERVES IMAGES AND NOTHING ELSE. A request for a path inside the root that is not a captured screenshot (a `.sqlite`, a `.json`, a dotfile) is REFUSED with its rostered code. The confinement is a directory AND a type: a root-confined server that will hand back any file in the tree is still an exfiltration surface.

Both routes are registered in every seam a read route must appear in and the roster arms pass: the production listener (JSON_ROUTES plus its non-POST guard where applicable), and `apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts` with its `live-document-proxy.test.ts` pin. The bidirectional roster arm in `http-listener-read-dispatch.test.ts` must pass without adding an exemption for a route this row serves - if the consumer has not landed yet, record the unconsumed-route census entry NAMING task-33ceae56 as the row that retires it, the way `/repository/bootstrap/read` did.

NO SECRET AND NO HOST PATH LEAKS TO THE BROWSER (epic rail 3). The served JSON carries no absolute filesystem path, no credential and no url with embedded userinfo; the capture route's refusals name a code, never the resolved path they refused. Assert with a positive control so the arm cannot pass vacuously.

MUTATION DRILL, quoted with its failing line: remove the root-confinement check from the capture route and confirm the traversal arm goes RED. Restore per global rail 13 - `git status --porcelain` first, back every mutated path up out of tree, restore FROM THE BACKUP rather than `git checkout --`, and prove by sha256 in a call separate from the restore.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file, so say that rather than quoting a bare root count line.
taskRails: SERVE, DO NOT RE-DERIVE. `PreviewReceiptV1` already carries url, screenshots, outcome and code; `readPreviewReceipt` is the production read surface. This row projects them and computes no new authority.

THE CAPTURE ROUTE IS A SECURITY BOUNDARY, NOT A FILE HELPER. Confinement to `.moe-next/previews/<goalId>/<sha>/` is enforced with the listener's EXISTING asset guards; a second file server with its own path logic is the defect this rail exists to prevent.
CONFINEMENT IS A DIRECTORY AND A TYPE. A root-confined server that returns any file under the root is still an exfiltration surface - serve captured images only.
READ-ONLY. Neither route writes, deletes, or creates anything, and neither one starts or stops a preview.
NO UI. The card, the controls, the words and the journey belong to task-33ceae56edc348e9864bc592430fa1d0.

THE ENFORCER IS `locateControlRoomAsset(root, method, requestPath)` in `apps/daemon/src/http/static-asset-host.ts:147-186`, over the pure policy in `static-asset-path-policy.ts`. Its FIXED ORDER, which the capture route inherits unchanged:
  judgeAssetMethod -> METHOD_INVALID (GET/HEAD only)
  decodeRequestPath -> ENCODING_INVALID (decode ONCE; a spelling that changes on a 2nd pass is refused, so `%252e%252e` dies here)
  judgeRequestPath  -> PATH_TRAVERSAL (`..`, `.`, empty segment, backslash, no leading `/`) then SEGMENT_INVALID (control chars, `<>:"|?*`, trailing dot/space, CON/PRN/NUL..., >260 chars, non-NFC, lone surrogate)

implementationPlan.description:
THE JSON READ (DoD 1). Create `apps/daemon/src/http/preview-read.ts` (+ a one-line `.js` bridge, the package convention).

An AUTHENTICATED read serving, for a goalId: `url`, `screenshots[]`, `outcome`, `code` at minimum - PROJECTED from `PreviewReceiptV1` through `readPreviewReceipt`, never re-derived (rail 1). Follow `apps/daemon/src/http/design-read.ts` as the shape precedent for a read route module.

EXACT-KEY RESPONSE: an unknown key and a missing key each refuse with the specific code AND the layer that refused. Reuse an already-rostered layer literal; introduce no new `*_LAYER`.

A GOAL WITH NO RECEIPT READS AS ABSENT, NOT AS A REFUSAL (DoD 1). Those are different facts to a card: absent means "no preview yet", refused means "something is wrong". Getting this backwards makes the consumer render an error for the ordinary case.

NO ABSOLUTE FILESYSTEM PATH IN THE RESPONSE (DoD 5, epic rail 3). `PreviewReceiptV1` carries a `pid` and the screenshots live under a real directory - project a RELATIVE reference the capture route can resolve, never the resolved host path. The browser has no use for a host path and every reason not to receive one.

READ-ONLY (rail 4): this module writes nothing, deletes nothing, and neither starts nor stops a preview.
implementationPlan.note:
THE JSON READ. `apps/daemon/src/http/preview-read.ts` (236 lines, under the 250 target) + the one-line `.js` bridge. Shape follows `design-read.ts` exactly: PATH const, module-private LAYER, closed codes roster, exact-key body decoder, optional port, `handleXReadRequest` returning REPLY-or-LISTENER_REFUSAL.

PROJECTION, NOT DERIVATION (rail 1). `readPreviewForGoal` re-READS every candidate through `readPreviewReceipt` (preview-ledger.ts:81) and decodes nothing itself. `projectionOf` copies NAMED members only, so a key the receipt grows later cannot leak through.
SERVED: code, decidedAt, goalId, outcome, receiptId, screenshots[], sha, url. DoD 1's four (url, screenshots, outcome, code) plus the three a card cannot render without — and `receiptId`, because it IS the `previewRef` a later `preview.decide` names (preview-daemon-edge.ts:225 `readPreviewReceipt(store, projectId, payload.previewRef)`); without it the consumer's approve/reject controls have no operand.
WITHHELD, deliberately: `pid` (a host process id), `projectId` (the principal's own — the browser cannot learn another project's from it) and `version` (store business). Stated in the module header so a later reader does not "helpfully" add them back.

WHY THE GOAL->RECEIPT INDEX EXISTS HERE. `readPreviewReceipt` is keyed by RECEIPT ID and `previewReceiptId = sha256(version,"receipt-id",projectId,goalId,sha)`, so a goalId alone cannot address it; the only landed goal-keyed reader (`createPreviewReceiptReader`, preview-daemon-edge.ts:120) returns the OUTCOME STRING alone. The walk here is the same shape (decisionsOf + kind/disposition/project/principal filter, later receipt wins) and, critically, the same authority: the filter picks CANDIDATES, `readPreviewReceipt` decides. I did not edit preview-daemon-edge.ts to share the walk — it is already 311 lines, over the 250 target, and a peer could be in it.

ABSENT vs REFUSED (DoD 1), the clause the step calls out as easy to get backwards:
  no committed receipt for the goal -> `{kind:"ABSENT", goalId}`. Not a refusal, no code, HTTP 200.
  a committed receipt that will not decode -> `{kind:"REFUSED", code:"PREVIEW_READ_RECEIPT_UNREADABLE", layer:"PREVIEW_READ"}`.
The ledger already distinguishes these (`PREVIEW_RECEIPT_NOT_FOUND` vs `PREVIEW_RECEIPT_INVALID`), so this is a forward, not a new judgement. NOT_FOUND on one candidate `continue`s (it is another goal's row); INVALID refuses the WHOLE read, because a ledger that cannot be read must not be reported as an empty one.

NO ABSOLUTE PATH (DoD 5). `PreviewScreenshot.path` is project-relative by the decoder's own construction — `parseScreenshots` (preview-receipt-contracts.ts:130-152) refuses any entry not prefixed `.moe-next/previews/<goalId>/<sha>/`, containing `..` or containing a backslash. So the response carries relative names the capture route resolves against a root the browser never sees. Nothing here calls `resolve`, `join` or `realpath`.

ONE THING THE PLAN DID NOT ASK FOR, and why I added it. The consumer renders `url` as a LINK. The runner writes it, but this route SERVES it, and a `javascript:` spelling would be script the operator clicks while a `http://user:pass@host` one is exactly the "url with embedded userinfo" DoD 5 forbids. `previewUrlIsServable` therefore re-judges protocol (http/https only) and userinfo (both empty) at the serving edge, and a url that fails REFUSES with `PREVIEW_READ_URL_UNSERVABLE` rather than being blanked — a card with no link is indistinguishable from a preview that never started. This is the enforcement point DoD 5's positive control will drive.

REFUSAL VOCABULARY. Three module-local codes (`PREVIEW_READ_CAPABILITY_DENIED`, `_RECEIPT_UNREADABLE`, `_URL_UNSERVABLE`) in an exported closed roster, the `DESIGN_READ_CODES` pattern. The layer stamp is a module-private `const LAYER = "PREVIEW_READ"` — NOT `PREVIEW_READ_LAYER`. That spelling is load-bearing: both boundary scanners require at least one character before the LAYER/LAYERS/BOUNDARIES token (`/^(export )?const ([A-Z0-9_]+(?:LAYERS|LAYER|BOUNDARIES))/`, boundary-roster.security.ts:603 and layer-visibility-cases.ts:64), so a bare `LAYER` is invisible to the security roster and owes it no backfill. Same as design-read.ts and environments-read.ts. NO new `*_LAYER` constant, NO twelfth asset code.
Transport faults use `LISTENER_PREVIEW_REQUEST_INVALID` / `LISTENER_PREVIEW_UNAVAILABLE`, registered in step 4.

EXACT KEYS. `previewReadBodyOf` accepts own enumerable keys EXACTLY `{goalId}` with a non-empty string. A body naming `projectId` is an UNKNOWN KEY, not an override — the project comes from the authenticated principal (`access.principal.projectId`) and never from the wire. Missing key, extra key, array, null, non-string and empty string all answer `LISTENER_PREVIEW_REQUEST_INVALID` at CONTROL_ROOM_LISTENER (stamped by `refuseRequest`), which is the layer that actually refused.

implementationPlan.description:
THE CAPTURE ROUTE (DoD 2 and 3) - the security boundary, and the reason this is a leaf row.

Serve the screenshot bytes CONFINED to `.moe-next/previews/<goalId>/<sha>/`, using the listener's EXISTING asset guards (rail 2). Do NOT write a second file server: the eleven codes already distinguish traversal, escape, bad encoding, bad segment, unknown type, oversize, missing and unreadable, and a hand-rolled confinement typically implements four of those and calls itself confined.

CONFINEMENT IS A DIRECTORY **AND** A TYPE (DoD 3, rail 3). A root-confined server that returns any file under the root is still an exfiltration surface - the previews root can sit beside stores, receipts and dotfiles. Serve CAPTURED IMAGES ONLY; anything else inside the root refuses `LISTENER_ASSET_TYPE_UNKNOWN`.
Decide type by CONTENT or by an allowlist of extensions you control - not by trusting the request. Say which in the note.

RESOLVE THEN COMPARE. Confinement is checked on the RESOLVED real path, after symlink resolution, against the resolved root - DoD 2 names a symlink pointing outside the root as its own refusal class, and a check done before resolution passes it.

READ-ONLY and METHOD-GUARDED: a non-GET refuses `LISTENER_ASSET_METHOD_INVALID`. The route creates, writes and deletes nothing (rail 4).

REFUSALS NAME A CODE, NEVER THE RESOLVED PATH (DoD 5). An error that echoes the path it refused hands the caller a filesystem probe - the refusal tells them the class, not the layout.
implementationPlan.note:
THE CAPTURE ROUTE. `apps/daemon/src/http/preview-capture-route.ts` (207 lines) + `.js` bridge, plus ONE additive edit to `http-listener-command-stream-routes.ts`.

NOT A SECOND FILE SERVER, and I can name exactly what I did and did not write (rail 2). The path judgement is the landed `locateControlRoomAsset` (static-asset-host.ts:147) over `static-asset-path-policy.ts`, called unchanged. `locatePreviewCapture` adds a NARROWING in front of it and NOTHING else — it contains no `realpath`, no containment comparison and no byte read. Grep-checkable: `isContainedBy` appears zero times in my module; there is still exactly ONE statement of confinement in this daemon, and step 6 drills that statement.

WHY I EXTENDED `serveAsset` INSTEAD OF COPYING IT. The response half of a static route — host check, refusal shape, HEAD, ETag/If-None-Match/304, the byte read, and writing the length ACTUALLY SENT rather than the stat's — is ~30 lines I would otherwise have mirrored, and a mirrored 304 path that drifts is a real bug. So `serveAsset` grew one OPTIONAL trailing parameter, `locate`, defaulting to `locateControlRoomAsset`; the capture route passes `locatePreviewCapture`. Additive, no call site changed, no existing behaviour moved, and `ControlRoomAssetDispatch` was already the return type. This is the smallest edit that leaves ONE response writer and ONE path judge for two roots.

THE NARROWING, in the order it runs, and the order IS the behaviour:
  1. `judgeAssetMethod` -> LISTENER_ASSET_METHOD_INVALID (405). GET/HEAD only; a POST/PUT/DELETE never reaches a path (rail 4: read-only, method-guarded).
  2. `decodeRequestPath` -> LISTENER_ASSET_ENCODING_INVALID. Decodes ONCE and refuses any spelling that changes on a second pass, so `%252e%252e%252f` dies here rather than becoming `..` later.
  3. `judgeRequestPath` -> LISTENER_ASSET_PATH_TRAVERSAL for `..`, `.`, an empty segment, a backslash or a missing leading `/`; then LISTENER_ASSET_SEGMENT_INVALID for control characters, `<>:"|?*`, trailing dot/space, reserved device names, >260 chars, non-NFC or a lone surrogate.
  4. SHAPE: EXACTLY three segments, `<goalId>/<sha>/<file>` -> LISTENER_ASSET_SEGMENT_INVALID otherwise. This is what makes the route confined to `.moe-next/previews/<goalId>/<sha>/` (DoD 2's literal wording) rather than merely to `.moe-next/previews`: a two- or four-segment path is not a capture and is refused before any syscall.
  5. TYPE -> LISTENER_ASSET_TYPE_UNKNOWN.
  6. only then `locateControlRoomAsset`: realpath, `isContainedBy(root, resolved)` -> LISTENER_ASSET_OUTSIDE_ROOT, stat -> LISTENER_ASSET_NOT_FOUND / LISTENER_ASSET_READ_FAILED / LISTENER_ASSET_TOO_LARGE.

HOW TYPE IS DECIDED — the step asks me to say. BY AN EXTENSION ALLOWLIST THIS MODULE OWNS, never by anything the request asserts: `PREVIEW_CAPTURE_CONTENT_TYPES = ["image/png"]`, applied to the type the shared CLOSED map resolves for the last segment. No Content-Type header, no Accept header and no sniffing participate. Not by content: reading bytes to decide whether to serve them means opening a file the caller may not be entitled to, which is the wrong order for a confinement decision — the type gate has to be answerable before the filesystem is touched.
`.svg` is EXCLUDED although it is an image: an SVG is a script carrier, and `preview-capture.ts:103` writes `type:"png"` only, so no real capture is one. `.js`, `.html` and `.css` are the exposure this narrowing actually closes — `.sqlite`, `.json` and dotfiles were already outside the shared map, but a root-confined server built on the unnarrowed locator WOULD have served a `.js` or an `.html` sitting under `.moe-next/previews`.

RESOLVE THEN COMPARE (DoD 2's symlink class). Containment is `isContainedBy(root.directory, realpathSync.native(join(root, ...segments)))` inside `locateControlRoomAsset` — realpath on BOTH sides. The root itself is proven with `realpathSync.native` in `resolvePreviewCaptureRoot`, so a symlinked previews directory is safe to serve from while a symlink INSIDE it pointing out is refused OUTSIDE_ROOT. A pre-resolution check passes exactly that case, which is why the check is not repeated in my module.

TYPE BEFORE DISK, deliberately, and it answers the step-7 question directly: a `.sqlite` inside the root and a `.sqlite` symlink pointing outside it BOTH answer TYPE_UNKNOWN, because nothing has been resolved yet. A type refusal therefore reveals nothing about whether the path exists. The converse order would make TYPE_UNKNOWN an existence oracle.

REFUSALS NAME A CODE, NEVER A PATH (DoD 5). `refuseRequest` (http-listener-command-stream-routes.ts:78-82) writes `{code, layer}` and its own comment says a refusal's `detail` never reaches the wire. `resolvePreviewCaptureRoot` does build a `detail` (the `refuseAssetRoot` shape demands one) but the handler discards it and returns the bare code — commented at that line so a later reader does not "improve" it into the response.

completionSummary:
The daemon now serves the preview receipt and its captured screenshot bytes over two authenticated read routes. 14 owned paths; production files 236 and 207 lines.

`/preview/read` (POST, exact-key `{goalId}`) PROJECTS `PreviewReceiptV1` through `readPreviewReceipt` and derives nothing: code, decidedAt, goalId, outcome, receiptId, screenshots[], sha, url. `receiptId` is included because it IS the `previewRef` a later `preview.decide` names. WITHHELD: pid (host process id), projectId (the principal's own), version. A goal with no receipt answers `{kind:"ABSENT"}`; a committed receipt that will not decode answers REFUSED with `PREVIEW_READ_RECEIPT_UNREADABLE` — absent and broken are different facts to a card. Screenshot paths are project-relative by the decoder's own construction, so no host path can reach the browser.
`/preview/capture/<goalId>/<sha>/<file>.png` (GET/HEAD) serves the bytes, confined by DIRECTORY **and** TYPE. It is NOT a second file server: `locateControlRoomAsset` is called unchanged, `isContainedBy` appears zero times in my code, and there is still one statement of confinement in this daemon. `serveAsset` grew one OPTIONAL `locate` parameter so both roots share one response writer (host check, HEAD, ETag/304, byte read, real content-length). The narrowing publishes `image/png` ALONE, by an allowlist this module owns, checked BEFORE any syscall — so `.js`/`.html`/`.css`/`.svg` under the previews root refuse TYPE_UNKNOWN, and a type refusal is never an existence oracle.
